method.shortlist: walk-forward P&L > 0, t >= 1.5, >= 50 trades, >= half of test folds profitable
rules: Only data from before the holdout was used to pick a family's settings; the holdout (last 15 days, same calendar cut for every coin as earlier labs) was run once per candidate with frozen settings.
Golden needs ALL of the following. (1) Made money on the holdout with a t-stat of at least 2.84, the strict bar that corrects for every candidate taken to the holdout (one-sided Bonferroni, 5%).

(2) Beat what is live on the same coin(s) on BOTH holdout profit and holdout t-stat: more profit than the most profitable live strategy trading that coin (including that coin's share of the all-coin strategies) and a higher t-stat than the live strategy with the best t-stat.

(3) Where older archive data exists for the coin (NEAR, DOGE, BNB, SOL from April-August; pooled for the all-coin scope), it also made money there with t >= 2 on at least 50 trades, with no re-tuning. If the rule cannot be run on the archive (e.g. it needs BTC prices the archive lacks), it cannot be golden.
(4) No more than 40% of its holdout profit came from a single day.
Pass = made money on the holdout with t >= 2 but missed at least one golden test. Fail = anything else.

Every result assumes $10 per trade, Kalshi taker fees (maker fee 1.75% for maker rules), fills at the quoted price at the end of the decision minute, and one bet per market. 'One minute late' re-runs the frozen rule with a 1-minute delay as a latency check; it is reported, not graded.
caveats: The live strategies were chosen in an earlier lab using this same holdout, so their holdout numbers are flattering; beating them here is a deliberately high bar.
The archive data was already used once (lab2) to check the plain live rule, so it is blind for the new families but not untouched. SOL's April-August data was used for SOL's blind test.
All of the edge depends on acting within about a minute of a spot move; the one-minute-late column shows how much survives a slow bot.
Backtest fills assume the quoted ask had enough size for a $10 order; real fills on thin books can be worse.
BTC/ETH spot data only starts on Aug 31, so rules that need BTC cannot be checked on the archive.
method.diagnostics: Added after the run as extra skeptic's checks; they do not change any status. 't by window' groups trades in the same 15-minute window (pooled scopes bet on several coins that move together, so the per-trade t overstates certainty); 't by day' uses daily totals. 'Paired vs live' is the extra holdout profit over the most profitable live rule on the same coin(s), with the t-stat of that difference per 15-minute window; 'paired vs control' does the same against the live model simply re-tuned on the search window (fv_ref).
summary: 0 of 22 candidates that reached the holdout are golden, 1 pass, 21 fail (strict bar t >= 2.84).
method.real_money: Real-money scoring: every result here (new strategies and the live baselines alike) is at about $0.50 a bet (1 to 10 whole contracts, Kalshi fees at that size), and each taker order counts only as often as real orders like it filled (fill model learned from 11,009 entries checked against Kalshi's trade records), with the real fill price instead of the candle price. Prices for NEAR, HYPE, DOGE and BNB are rebuilt from Coinbase's public trade list.

families.name: Live model, re-tuned (control)
families.idea: The model already live (bell-curve fair value vs the ask), re-tuned on a wider grid. It is the control: a new idea has to do better than simply re-tuning what we have.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Live model, re-tuned (control) (10c edge, larger of 1h/4h vol, vol x0.8): $27 at t = 1.59 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Fat-tail fair value
families.idea: Price the contract with a fat-tailed (Student-t) distribution instead of the bell curve, so big moves before the close count as more likely. Long shots have been winning live.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Fat-tail fair value (7c edge, tail thickness 3, 1h+4h vol blend, vol x1.25): $21 at t = 1.06 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$6 (paired t = -0.35).

families.name: Bootstrap fair value
families.idea: No formula: the chance of finishing above the strike is read off this coin's own recent history of similar-sized moves (last 7 or 21 days of 1-minute prices).
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Bootstrap fair value (9c edge, last 7 days of moves, vol x1.1): $16 at t = 0.98 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$10 (paired t = -0.58).

families.name: Recalibrated fair value
families.idea: Stretch or squash the model's probabilities toward or away from 50% (a calibration slope) to correct a model that is systematically over- or under-confident.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Better volatility
families.idea: Same model, but measure volatility better: exponentially weighted, high/low range (Parkinson), jump-robust (bipower), shorter windows, or the larger of 1h and 4h.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Better volatility (8c edge, weighted+4h vol blend, vol x0.7): $-0 at t = -0.02 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$27 (paired t = -2.04).

families.name: Time-of-day volatility
families.idea: Crypto is calmer at some hours than others. Scale volatility by how this 15-minute slot of the day has behaved over the previous two weeks.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Time-of-day volatility (9c edge, time-of-day weighted vol, vol x0.8): $26 at t = 1.68 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$1 (paired t = -0.08).

families.name: Settlement-average timing
families.idea: Kalshi settles on an average of the final minute, which leaves less real time for the price to move than the clock says. Shorten (or lengthen) the time left in the model.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Settlement-average timing (9c edge, time left -0.33 min): $22 at t = 1.29 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$4 (paired t = -0.24).

families.name: Momentum-aware fair value
families.idea: Assume part of the coin's last few minutes of movement carries on (or reverses) and build that drift into the fair value.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: BTC catch-up fair value
families.idea: If BTC (ETH for BTC itself) has just moved more than this coin, assume the coin partly catches up and build that into the fair value.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · BTC catch-up fair value (20c edge, BTC catch-up x-0.5 since the open): $0 at t = 0.02 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$27 (paired t = -1.44).

families.name: Dynamic edge
families.idea: Ask for a bigger (or smaller) mispricing depending on minutes left, the bid-ask spread and the price level, instead of one fixed 12-cent gap.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Dynamic edge (8c edge, +0c early, +0.0x spread, vol x0.8): $19 at t = 1.18 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$8 (paired t = -0.56).

families.name: Volatility-regime filter
families.idea: Only trade when short-term volatility is clearly above (rising) or below (calming) the 4-hour level.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Spread / stale-quote filter
families.idea: Only trade when the Kalshi spread is tight, and/or only when the quote has (or has not) just moved, and/or contracts actually traded that minute.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Spread / stale-quote filter (8c edge, spread <= 10c, traded that minute, vol x0.8): $19 at t = 1.18 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$8 (paired t = -0.56).

families.name: Fresh spot move, lagging quote
families.idea: Only trade when the gap was opened by a spot move in the last 1-2 minutes (the model jumped) and, optionally, the Kalshi quote has not yet followed.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: BTC confirmation
families.idea: Only take the trade when BTC (ETH for BTC) has moved the same way since the open, or only when it has moved the other way (contrarian).
families.finding: Best: ZEC · BTC confirmation (8c edge, BTC moved the other way, vol x0.8): $5 at t = 0.37 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$22 (paired t = -1.42).

families.name: Jump trigger
families.idea: Only trade right after a sudden 1-minute jump in spot (when Kalshi is most likely to lag), or only in calm minutes.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Jump trigger (7c edge, 1-min move < 1 sd, vol x0.8): $9 at t = 0.53 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$18 (paired t = -1.06).

families.name: Session / weekday filter
families.idea: Live model limited to certain hours of the day (Asia, Europe, US, late US) or to weekdays or weekends only.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Previous-window filter
families.idea: Only take the fair-value trade when the previous 15-minute window moved the same way as the bet (trend) or the opposite way (reversal), by at least a set number of standard deviations.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Ensemble of live-style models
families.idea: Run several fair-value models side by side (bell curve, blended volatility, edge vs the bid, fat-tail) and take the first signal, or only signals two models agree on. One bet per market.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Ensemble of live-style models (10c edge, fv+v2, first signal, vol x0.8): $23 at t = 1.49 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$4 (paired t = -0.43).

families.name: Exit before settlement
families.idea: Buy on the same mispricing, then sell back at the bid once the price has converged to fair value, hit a profit target, or at a set minute, instead of holding to the close. Pays the taker fee both ways.
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Exit before settlement (8c edge, sell once the bid reaches fair value, vol x0.8): $30 at t = 2.15 on the holdout (pass). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: +$3 (paired t = 0.2).

families.name: Limit order at fair value minus edge
families.idea: Instead of paying the ask, rest a bid at (fair value - edge) for a few minutes; filled only if a seller comes down to it. Cheaper fee, but misses trades and risks bad fills.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Live model as a maker
families.idea: The live model's signal, but executed by resting a bid at the best bid (+1c) for 1-3 minutes instead of buying at the ask.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Edge-scaled stakes
families.idea: Live model, but bet more when the model's edge is bigger (fractional Kelly), capped at 2-5x the average stake. Stakes are scaled so the average is about $10, to stay comparable.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Per-coin tuning with shrinkage
families.idea: One rule for all 9 coins, but each coin gets its own settings, chosen by that coin's own results plus the all-coin average (shrinkage), so thin data can't drive it alone.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Ensemble of the best survivors
families.idea: For each coin, combine the 2-3 families with the best walk-forward record into one first-to-fire rule (one bet per market).
families.finding: Best: ZEC · Ensemble of the best survivors: $21 at t = 1.07 on the holdout (fail). Versus the re-tuned live model on the same markets: -$5 (paired t = -0.33).
